title: Lay a sterile surgical instrument set on a sterile field without touching its unsterile border or the table
instruction: Move the four sterile instruments from the sterile rack onto the blue sterile field, laid flat and apart. The grippers start sterile too: nothing may touch the orange border or the bare table.
context: Laying instruments out on a sterile field is routine work for medical assistants (O*NET 31-9092, about 760,000 US jobs, whose listed tasks include preparing treatment rooms and sterilizing and setting out instruments for procedures), surgical technologists (29-2055, about 110,000) and operating-room nurses. On a sterile drape the outer inch is not sterile, and neither is the table around it: an instrument that touches either, or is handled by a gripper (a hand, in practice) that has, is contaminated and has to be replaced, however it is placed afterwards, so contamination is judged over the whole handling, not only the end layout. Surgical-site infections are among the commonest hospital-acquired infections.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. A sterile field stands on the table centred at x 0.40, y 0.14: a flat rigid panel 300 x 440 mm, 3 mm thick, blue inside with a 25.4 mm (1 inch) orange border band all round (it stands in for a cloth drape). Beside it, centred at x 0.35, y 0.50, a stainless rack (tray 250 x 200 mm) holds four instruments lying flat on silicone rests, side by side 58 mm apart, with their working ends toward +y: needle holder (Mayo-Hegar, 6 in, 152 mm, 70 g), Metzenbaum scissors (7 in, 180 mm, 50 g), Rochester-Pean forceps (6.25 in, 160 mm, 60 g, closed on the ratchet) and a no. 4 scalpel handle (135 mm, 22 g, no blade). All are closed, rigid, free on the rack. Sterile at the start: all four instruments, the whole rack (tray and rests), the blue inside of the field, and both grippers' finger pads (as if in sterile covers). Not sterile: the orange border band and the bare tabletop everywhere outside the panel and the rack; the rest of the robot is not scored.
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each, one per instrument. An instrument counts when (1) a gripper has picked it up, (2) it is still sterile, and (3) it now lies on the sterile area: every point of it inside the blue area, flat (within 5 degrees), resting on the panel, not in a gripper, at least 8 mm from the other instruments. Contamination is for good (a red tag appears on the instrument): the instrument can no longer score and 1.0 is out of reach, however it is moved afterwards. An instrument is contaminated when any surface point comes within 1.5 mm of a nonsterile surface (the border band's top face, or the bare tabletop), at any time; or when a gripper whose finger pads have themselves come within 1.5 mm of a nonsterile surface touches it (a pad face within 2 mm of its bounding box), before or after it is laid. A gripper's own contamination is for good, but costs nothing until it touches an instrument. Carrying an instrument over the border without touching is fine; no heading or position in the layout is required. Full score 1.0 (ends the run) only once all four steps hold, no instrument is contaminated, both grippers are at least 3 cm from every instrument and everything is still (2 mm, 2 degrees) for 1 s without a break; any lapse restarts the second and the step points stop at 0.8. 0 if an instrument falls off the table.
reset_notes: Put the four instruments back on the rack rests as described in the setup; nothing on the field needs resetting (the contamination record of instruments and grippers, and the red tags, restart with the episode).
fidelity: Instruments are rigid, closed, at catalog lengths; cross-sections and masses are typical values, ring holes modelled. The drape is cloth in reality; here a flat rigid 3 mm panel with the border drawn on it. Contamination is judged in task code from poses (instrument surface and finger-pad faces within 1.5 mm of the band or the bare table, latched); sterile covers on the grippers are not modelled, and the red tag is a visual only. Convex colliders, 240 Hz physics.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (left arm moved around the rack, nothing picked up, no contamination); demo: 1.0 (success at step 1026, no instrument or gripper contaminated)
